questions_before_investigating: Does the Festival Box enquiry OTP step actually gate submission, or can `submit` be called without a valid OTP?
Is the honeypot check ordered before or after validation/OTP verification, and does that ordering leak a bot-detection oracle?
Is the per-IP/per-email throttle atomic under concurrency, or a TOCTOU count-then-insert race?
Does getRemoteAddr() reflect the real client IP in production, or the reverse proxy's IP (which would turn the per-IP cap into a global cap)?
Is the coupon-copy endpoint's sponsorSlug validated against anything real, or does it accept arbitrary attacker-chosen strings that grow the table unbounded?
Does the public Festival Box edition page (`festival-editions.ts`) actually have any live sponsors wired to real Workspaces, i.e. does the coupon-copy telemetry event ever fire in production today?
Are all marketing/legal/blog routes claimed in App.tsx actually registered, in the right order relative to the `/:handle` catch-all?
What happens when a visitor hits an unknown single-segment path like `/randomtypo` — does it 404, or silently 200 through the portfolio catch-all?
Do all 9 legal-page routes have real backing content files, or do any 404/render empty?
Is there a controller-level test for FestivalCouponCopyController, given the task flagged '(no test)'?
Does an existing (already-registered, already-verified) brand get dead-ended by the Festival OTP flow the way F-0601 dead-ended signup?
Can the same verified OTP be replayed to back more than one enquiry submission?
Is the coupon-copy 204-always contract actually indistinguishable for a bad sponsor vs a good one (no enumeration oracle)?
Does the dev-only `/dev/motion-skills` route actually get excluded from a production build?
Do the blog and legal routes render a real 404 (NotFoundPage) for unknown slugs, or something else?

features.name: Festival Box enquiry + OTP (POST /festival-enquiries/send-otp, /festival-enquiries)
features.user_type: Anonymous public visitor (brand or creator with no Influora account)
features.purpose: Capture a sales lead / roster application from the /festival-box marketing page, gated by an emailed OTP so the submitter provably controls the email address, with abuse controls since it is the only unauthenticated INSERT in the app.
features.classification: IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED (raised to VERIFIED WORKING for the unit-level flows actually exercised by the existing test suite, which was executed in this audit)
features.entry_point: FE: src/components/site/FestivalEnquiryForm.tsx (rendered from src/pages/festival-box.tsx). BE: FestivalEnquiryController.java:48 (sendOtp) and :62 (submit).
features.flow: FestivalEnquiryForm.handleSubmit -> festivalEnquiry.sendOtp(email) [src/lib/api.ts:6886 -> POST /festival-enquiries/send-otp] -> FestivalEnquiryController.sendOtp:48 -> BrandEmailOtpService.sendOtpForPublicForm (BrandEmailOtpService.java:171-181, unconditional delivery unlike signup's sendOtp) -> EmailOtpChallengeRepository.save (new EmailOtpChallenge row, otpHash + expiresAt) -> Msg91EmailClient (via OtpEmailDispatcher) mails the code (dev: log-only). Visitor enters code -> FestivalEnquiryForm.confirmCode -> festivalEnquiry.submit({...pending, otp}) [api.ts:6898 -> POST /festival-enquiries] -> FestivalEnquiryController.submit:62 -> brandEmailOtpService.verifyOtp(email, otp) (runs in its OWN transaction, outside FestivalEnquiryService's, deliberately per FestivalEnquiryController.java:65-71 javadoc, to keep the attempts++ lockout from being rolled back) -> on success -> FestivalEnquiryService.submit (FestivalEnquiryService.java:128) validates cross-field rules by type, runs honeypot check (AFTER validation, deliberately, per [Kabir F-2] comment at line 129-138), hashes IP via FestivalClientIpHasher, calls enforceThrottle (per-IP tiered + per-email caps via AbuseThrottleService.tryConsume, REQUIRES_NEW so refused attempts still consume budget), builds a FestivalEnquiry entity (brand or creator variant), applies provenance (utm*, ipHash, user-agent), saves via FestivalEnquiryRepository, returns SubmitEnquiryResponse{received:true,message}.
features.api: POST /api/v1/festival-enquiries/send-otp (SendEnquiryOtpRequest{email} -> SendEmailOtpResponse), POST /api/v1/festival-enquiries (SubmitEnquiryRequest{type,edition,name,email,phone,company,website,tier,productCategory,instagramHandle,followers,city,message,utm*,honeypot,otp} -> SubmitEnquiryResponse{received,message}). Both permitAll, named as exact verb+path (SecurityConfig.java:222-223, 238-239), never a `/festival-**` wildcard.
features.database: festival_enquiries table (migration V20260905130000__festival_enquiries.sql), inserted via FestivalEnquiryRepository.save(FestivalEnquiry entity). email_otp_challenges table (existing, shared with signup) inserted/updated by BrandEmailOtpService. No update path — every enquiry is an insert-only row read later by admin (out of this domain's scope).
features.state_machine: OTP challenge: none -> issued (unverified, expiresAt=+5min) -> [verifyOtp] verified=true (idempotent; a second verifyOtp call with the same still-valid code re-succeeds, since verifyOtp does not check challenge.isVerified() before matching) OR attempts++ up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 -> TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS. Enquiry: none -> submitted (single terminal state; no admin-facing status transition in this domain).
features.authn: None (permitAll, unauthenticated by design — the whole point of the page).
features.working_condition: A visitor fills the form, receives a 6-digit code by email within OTP_TTL_SECONDS=300s, enters it, and the enquiry row is persisted with type-correct required fields (BRAND needs company; CREATOR needs a validated Instagram handle), honeypot empty, under both throttle caps (6/hr per-IP tiered, 3/hr per-email), and the OTP verifies against the newest live challenge for that email.
features.failure_conditions: Wrong/expired OTP -> INVALID_OTP/OTP_EXPIRED/TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS (400/410/429) with pending form data preserved client-side (FestivalEnquiryForm.tsx:147-154). Honeypot filled -> same 200 success response as a real submission, row never written (FestivalEnquiryService.java:158-161). Throttle tripped -> 429 TOO_MANY_ENQUIRIES, does not reveal which cap tripped. Unconfigured mailer (non-dev) -> 503 EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED at the send-otp step, applied identically for every address (BrandEmailOtpService.java:344-353) so it cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
features.security_conditions: Honeypot check runs AFTER field validation (deliberate fix for [Kabir F-2] enumeration oracle: previously a bot could binary-search field names because pre-validation honeypot-first gave a distinguishable 200-with-trap vs 400-without-trap). Two-key atomic throttle (IP tiers /64,/56,/48 with escalating caps + canonicalized-email, `+tag` stripped) via AbuseThrottleService.tryConsume, replacing a prior TOCTOU COUNT-then-INSERT race (documented at FestivalEnquiryService.java:260-269, closed by V20260905190000 migration; FestivalEnquiryServiceThrottleConcurrencyTest cited as the real, non-mocked proof — not independently re-run in this pass). getRemoteAddr() is trusted only because application.yml sets forward-headers-strategy: native (Tomcat RemoteIpValve rewrites it from X-Forwarded-For validated against server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies) — this audit did not independently verify that yml setting in the RC tree beyond the javadoc's own claim; NOT independently re-confirmed here (time-boxed). Website field scheme-validated (http/https only) to prevent stored javascript: XSS rendered later in the admin console. OTP verified in its own transaction outside submit's, specifically to avoid noRollbackFor interactions undoing the attempts++ lockout.
features.tests: FestivalEnquiryServiceTest (executed in this audit: `mvn -q -o -Dtest=FestivalEnquiryServiceTest test`, exit code 0, log output confirms honeypot-reject, per-IP-tier throttle, per-email throttle, BRAND and CREATOR builds all exercised). FestivalEnquiryRepositoryQueryTest (repository-level, not re-run). FestivalClientIpHasherTiersTest (not re-run). No FestivalEnquiryControllerTest was found — the controller's OTP-before-honeypot ordering and the split-transaction behavior described in its javadoc (FestivalEnquiryController.java:65-79) are NOT exercised by any web-layer test found; only the service layer is. BrandEmailOtpServiceTest exists for the shared OTP primitive but was not re-run in this pass.
features.production_conditions: MSG91 email client must be configured (non-dev) or every send-otp call 503s. forward-headers-strategy: native must be set (claimed in application.yml, spot-checked via javadoc only, not independently grepped in this pass) for the per-IP throttle to bound real distinct visitors rather than the reverse proxy's single IP.
features.evidence: FestivalEnquiryController.java (full read), FestivalEnquiryService.java (full read), BrandEmailOtpService.java (full read), FestivalEnquiryDtos.java (full read), FestivalEnquiryForm.tsx (full read), src/lib/api.ts:6844-6920 (festivalEnquiry client), SecurityConfig.java grep for the exact permitAll matchers, and a live `mvn -Dtest=FestivalEnquiryServiceTest test` run (exit 0) in the RC tree.
known_issues: verifyOtp() (called directly by FestivalEnquiryController, not the register-path's requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail) does not consume/invalidate the challenge on success — the same still-valid OTP can be replayed to back more than one /festival-enquiries submission within its 5-minute TTL and while attempts<3, since verifyOtp only checks expiry+attempts+hash, not challenge.isVerified(). Mitigated in practice by the 3/hour per-email submission cap, but the OTP does not strictly prove one-code-one-submission the way registration's requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail (spend-on-use) does.

No controller-level (@WebMvcTest or MockMvc) test exists for FestivalEnquiryController; the split-transaction ordering the class's own javadoc calls load-bearing (OTP verified outside submit's @Transactional boundary) is only indirectly protected by the service-level test and by code reading, not by an executed regression test of the controller wiring itself.

This audit did not re-run FestivalEnquiryServiceThrottleConcurrencyTest (the cited proof of the atomic-throttle fix) or independently grep application.yml's forward-headers-strategy value; both claims are taken from in-code javadoc, which is context, not proof, per this audit's own evidence rules — flagged here as a verification gap rather than asserted as true.
required_fixes: If one-OTP-one-submission is an intended invariant, either invalidate/consume the challenge in FestivalEnquiryController.submit after a successful verifyOtp (mirroring requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail's spend semantics), or document explicitly that OTP here only proves current mailbox control at verification time, not per-submission.

Add a MockMvc/WebMvcTest for FestivalEnquiryController to lock in the OTP-verified-before-honeypot-check ordering and the two-transaction split, since that ordering is called out in its own comments as security-load-bearing but is not directly tested.

features.name: Festival coupon-copied telemetry (permitAll)
features.purpose: Fire-and-forget counter of tap-to-copy coupon events per sponsor per day, sold to sponsors as an engagement metric (with a documented caveat that it is not a trustworthy per-visitor count).
features.entry_point: FE: src/pages/festival-box-edition.tsx:161 (reportCouponCopied, called from the tap-to-copy handler around line 589/622). BE: FestivalCouponCopyController.java:42.
features.flow: Shopper taps a coupon code on /festival-box/:edition -> copyTextToClipboard succeeds -> reportCouponCopied(editionKey, sponsorSlug, couponCode) fires a raw navigator.sendBeacon (falling back to fetch with keepalive) directly to `${FESTIVAL_API_BASE_URL}/festival/coupon-copied` — this bypasses BOTH existing FE API layers (src/lib/api.ts and meera-api.ts) with a third, ad-hoc client, per festival-box-edition.tsx:148-182 -> FestivalCouponCopyController.recordCopy:42 (permitAll) -> FestivalCouponCopyService.recordCopy (FestivalCouponCopyService.java:137): normalizes+checks `edition` against FestivalEditions constant (silent drop if unknown), checks `sponsorSlug` against WorkspaceRepository.existsBySlugAndType(slug, BRAND) (silent drop if unrecognized), applies a per-origin-per-sponsor-per-day influence cap via AbuseThrottleService, then FestivalCouponCopyRepository.recordCopy upserts a (edition, sponsor_slug, bucket_day) counter row. Controller always returns 204 No Content regardless of outcome.
features.api: POST /api/v1/festival/coupon-copied (RecordCouponCopyRequest{edition,sponsorSlug,couponCode} -> 204, no body). permitAll, exact verb+path (SecurityConfig.java:254-255).
features.database: festival_coupon_copies table (migration V20260905170000__festival_coupon_copies.sql), unique key (edition, sponsor_slug, bucket_day), upserted via FestivalCouponCopyRepository.recordCopy. Reads workspaces table via WorkspaceRepository.existsBySlugAndType for sponsor recognition.
features.state_machine: N/A (idempotent daily-bucket counter increment; no per-event row, no lifecycle).
features.working_condition: A shopper on a LIVE edition page with at least one real, provisioned sponsor (a Workspace of type BRAND whose slug matches the page's hand-authored FestivalSponsor.slug) taps a coupon; the counter for that (edition, sponsorSlug, today) increments by exactly one, bounded by the per-origin daily cap.
features.failure_conditions: Unknown edition or unrecognized sponsorSlug -> silent no-op, still 204 (no enumeration signal by design). Per-origin daily cap (20, tiered up for coarser IPv6 prefixes) exceeded -> silent no-op, still 204. Network failure / sendBeacon unavailable -> swallowed entirely client-side, never surfaced to the shopper (by design, since it must never block the clipboard copy).
features.security_conditions: No honeypot (fire-and-forget by design). Bean validation is a strict allow-list charset (edition ^[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$, sponsorSlug ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, couponCode ^[A-Z0-9_-]{1,50}$) because these values are bound into a native SQL statement's parameters (FestivalCouponCopyRepository#recordCopy per DTO javadoc) rather than sanitized. [Kabir H-1] fix: edition is checked against a real registry (FestivalEditions) before the DB is touched at all, closing a previously unbounded-row-growth hole where an attacker-chosen edition string (in a table keyed on (edition, sponsor_slug, bucket_day)) could mint unlimited rows. [Kabir M-1/M-2] per-origin-per-sponsor daily influence cap exists specifically to bound how far one actor can move a number sold to a sponsor, not to rate-limit requests. Documented, accepted, NOT-closed timing side-channel: a recognized sponsor does more DB work than an unrecognized one, so response timing can distinguish a real sponsor slug from a fake one — the service's own javadoc argues this is moot because GET /workspaces/slug-check already answers that question exactly and for free; this audit did not independently verify that endpoint's permitAll status in this pass.
features.tests: FestivalCouponCopyServiceTest (executed in this audit: `mvn -q -o -Dtest=FestivalCouponCopyServiceTest test`, exit 0; log output confirms unrecognized-edition drop, unrecognized-sponsor drop, per-origin cap drop, and successful record paths were all exercised). FestivalCouponCopyDtosTest (bean-validation charset test, also run, exit 0). FestivalCouponCopyRepositoryConcurrencyTest and FestivalBoxCouponConstraintIntegrationTest exist but were NOT re-run in this pass. No FestivalCouponCopyControllerTest exists anywhere in the RC tree — confirmed by a targeted find across influora-api/src/test — matching the task's own note of '(no test)' at the controller layer specifically; the controller's 204-always contract and its getRemoteAddr()-only (never X-Forwarded-For) wiring are unverified at the web layer.
features.production_conditions: Requires at least one real Workspace of type BRAND provisioned via FestivalSponsorProvisioningService whose slug matches the FestivalSponsor.slug hand-authored in src/content/festival-editions.ts for a copy to actually be counted.
features.evidence: FestivalCouponCopyController.java (full read), FestivalCouponCopyService.java (full read, including its own javadoc's admission of the wiring gap below), FestivalCouponCopyDtos.java (full read), src/content/festival-editions.ts (full read, lines 1-141), src/pages/festival-box-edition.tsx:140-220 (full read), a find across influora-api/src/test confirming no controller test exists, and a live `mvn -Dtest=FestivalCouponCopyServiceTest,FestivalCouponCopyDtosTest test` run (exit 0).
known_issues: As of this audit, Edition 01 (`mumbai-2026`, the only edition in FESTIVAL_EDITIONS) has `sponsors: []` in src/content/festival-editions.ts (line 126) — the file's own header states this is deliberate and truthful ("Edition 01 is still being sold; no brand has signed"). Consequence: the tap-to-copy UI that calls reportCouponCopied() has no sponsor to render on the live page today, so this telemetry event is currently UNREACHABLE from real user interaction in production, despite being fully implemented and unit-tested end to end.

FestivalCouponCopyService.java's own javadoc (lines 69-73) states the FE's sponsorSlug (a hand-authored content id in festival-editions.ts, 'NOT wired to any workspace') 'must equal that sponsor's workspace slug for copies to actually be counted — that wiring is outside this task's backend-only scope and is called out here rather than silently assumed.' This is a self-reported integration gap, not independently falsified further in this pass: when a sponsor IS eventually added to the content file, there is no compile-time or runtime check that its slug matches a real Workspace slug, so a copy-paste/typo in the content file would silently produce zero recorded copies with no error anywhere (matching the class's documented no-enumeration-signal 204-always contract).

reportCouponCopied() in festival-box-edition.tsx uses a THIRD, ad-hoc fetch/sendBeacon client (neither src/lib/api.ts nor meera-api.ts), duplicating base-URL resolution (`import.meta.env?.VITE_API_BASE_URL`) outside the codebase's two existing API-layer conventions — a maintenance/consistency issue, not a functional defect, per the 'Two API layers' known trap in this repo.

No FestivalCouponCopyControllerTest exists — the web-layer contract (always 204, getRemoteAddr()-only IP resolution) is implemented per the controller's own comments but not regression-tested at that layer.
required_fixes: Add a lightweight build-time or startup check (or at minimum a documented manual runbook step) that validates every FestivalSponsor.slug in festival-editions.ts against a real Workspace slug before an edition is marked LIVE, so a sponsor never silently gets zero counted copies.

Add a FestivalCouponCopyControllerTest (MockMvc) asserting the always-204 contract for malformed vs well-formed-but-unrecognized requests, and that getRemoteAddr() (not X-Forwarded-For) is what's passed to the service.

Consider routing reportCouponCopied() through the existing src/lib/api.ts http client (with a raw-fetch/sendBeacon fallback kept only where keepalive semantics require it) rather than a third ad-hoc client.

features.name: Public creator surfaces /c/:username/verified, single-segment catch-all /:handle portfolio, * NotFound; dev-only /dev/motion-skills
features.user_type: Anonymous public visitor / search & AI crawler; developer (motion-skills route only)
features.purpose: Public, no-auth verified-metrics page and the @handle creator portfolio page (the platform's main indexable public surface), plus a catch-all 404 and a dev-only internal test route.
features.entry_point: App.tsx:875 (/c/:username/verified -> CreatorVerifiedMetricsPage), App.tsx:882 (/:handle -> CreatorPortfolioPublicPage), App.tsx:883 (* -> NotFoundPage), App.tsx:691-693 (dev-only route).
features.flow: CreatorPortfolioPublicPage (src/pages/creator-portfolio-public.tsx:152): reads the whole first path segment as `handle`; if it does NOT start with '@', sets error='Page not found' WITHOUT ever calling the API (line 206-210) and renders an inline not-found block (lines 271-288) — this is a client-side render, HTTP 200 from the server (app-shell.html via public/_redirects' `/* /app-shell.html 200` wildcard, since /:handle has no physical dist/ file). If the handle DOES start with '@', it calls api.portfolio.getPublic(username); a 404/error from the API renders the same inline block with 'We could not find this creator.' Because /:handle is registered as a SINGLE-SEGMENT catch-all ahead of the `*` route, ANY unmatched single-segment path (e.g. /randomtypo, not just /@unknownhandle) is captured here and gets this component's inline not-found state — the dedicated NotFoundPage component at the `*` route (line 883) is only ever reached for multi-segment unmatched paths. Dev-only route: gated by `{import.meta.env.DEV && (...)}` (line 691), a build-time constant that Vite strips in a production build, so JSX for that route (and, per standard Vite dead-code elimination, DevMotionSkillsPage's import) should not ship in the prod bundle — not independently confirmed by inspecting a built prod bundle in this pass.

This is functionally similar to a real 404 for the visitor (both say 'not found') but is architecturally inconsistent with blog/post.tsx's pattern of explicitly delegating to `<NotFoundPage />` for an unknown identifier (see the Blog feature above), and means NotFoundPage's own copy/JSON-LD/whatever-it-renders is effectively dead code for any single-segment URL.

known_issues: Any unmatched single-segment path (not just a real-looking @handle) is swallowed by the /:handle catch-all and rendered via CreatorPortfolioPublicPage's inline not-found block rather than ever reaching the dedicated NotFoundPage component at the `*` route — this is by design per the route ordering comments, but means NotFoundPage is effectively unreachable for any single-path-segment URL, which is architecturally inconsistent with how blog/post.tsx handles its own unknown-identifier case (explicit `return <NotFoundPage />`).
required_fixes: If NotFoundPage carries meta/JSON-LD/copy that should apply uniformly across the site, consider having CreatorPortfolioPublicPage's non-'@'-prefixed branch delegate to <NotFoundPage /> directly (mirroring blog/post.tsx) instead of maintaining a second, page-local not-found UI — purely a consistency/maintenance improvement, not a functional defect given app-shell.html's noindex status.

findings.title: Festival coupon-copy telemetry is unreachable in production: Edition 01 ships with zero sponsors
findings.evidence: src/content/festival-editions.ts:110-129 — FESTIVAL_EDITIONS['mumbai-2026'].sponsors is a committed empty array, with an explicit code comment ('NO FABRICATED SPONSORS... Edition 01 is still being sold; no brand has signed') confirming this is the real, current, intentional state, not a stub.
findings.impact: The fully-implemented, unit-tested FestivalCouponCopyController/Service/Repository stack (backed by a real migration and abuse controls) has no live caller: the tap-to-copy UI on /festival-box/mumbai-2026 has no sponsor to render, so reportCouponCopied() never fires from a real visitor today. Anyone reading 'coupon-copy telemetry: WORKING' from code alone would be wrong about what is actually observable in production right now.
findings.recommended_fix: No code fix required — this is a content/business-timing gap, not a bug. Track it as a go-live gate item: coupon-copy metrics cannot be demonstrated to a sponsor until at least one FestivalSponsor entry is added with a slug matching a real provisioned Workspace.
findings.verification_required: Re-check src/content/festival-editions.ts once Edition 01 sponsors are actually signed, and confirm at that point that each sponsor's slug matches a real Workspace slug (see MKT-02).

findings.title: No automated check that a Festival Box sponsor's content-file slug matches its real Workspace slug
findings.evidence: FestivalCouponCopyService.java:61-73 (javadoc, self-reported gap: 'the sponsorSlug used on the public page... currently a hand-authored content id, NOT wired to any workspace... that wiring is outside this task's backend-only scope and is called out here rather than silently assumed'). Cross-referenced against src/content/festival-editions.ts's FestivalSponsor.slug field comment ('Stable id, used as a React key and in the click-tracking path') which confirms the FE slug is hand-authored, not fetched from any backend registry.
findings.impact: When a real sponsor is eventually added to festival-editions.ts, a typo'd or stale slug (e.g. workspace slug changes after provisioning, or a copy-paste error) would produce silent zero-counted copies with no error surfaced anywhere — the endpoint's own documented no-enumeration-signal 204-always contract makes this class of mismatch invisible in both the browser network tab and any log a non-engineer would look at.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a lightweight CI or pre-launch check comparing every FestivalSponsor.slug in festival-editions.ts against WorkspaceRepository for existence (e.g. a script hitting a read-only admin endpoint, or a build-time fixture test), or add server-side logging distinguishing 'sponsor recognized' vs 'sponsor not recognized' at a level an on-call engineer (not just DEBUG) would notice before a sponsor's report period ends.
findings.verification_required: Confirm whether any such check already exists elsewhere in the admin/provisioning code (e.g. FestivalSponsorProvisioningServiceTest) that this pass did not open — this finding is based on the coupon-copy service's own documentation of the gap, not an independent repository-wide search for a mitigating check.

findings.title: Festival Box enquiry OTP is not consumed on use; the same code can back more than one submission
findings.evidence: BrandEmailOtpService.verifyOtp (BrandEmailOtpService.java:376-424) checks challenge.getExpiresAt() and challenge.getAttempts() but never challenge.isVerified() before matching the hash, and sets verified=true unconditionally on match without invalidating the row for future reads; contrast with requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail (lines 443-469), the register-path method that explicitly calls otpRepository.clearVerifiedForEmail(normalized) after use. FestivalEnquiryController.submit (line 77) calls verifyOtp directly, never requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail.
findings.impact: A visitor (or anyone who intercepts/knows the code within its 5-minute TTL and before 3 wrong attempts) could submit the Festival Box form more than once using a single mailed OTP, weakening the 'proves the submitter controls this email, once' guarantee to 'proved control of this email at some point in the last 5 minutes.' Bounded in practice by the pre-existing 3-per-hour-per-email submission throttle, so the practical abuse ceiling is low, but the guarantee described by the feature's own security posture (an OTP-gated lead form) is slightly weaker than it reads.
findings.recommended_fix: If one-code-one-submission is intended, have FestivalEnquiryController (or FestivalEnquiryService) call a consume-on-success variant (or explicitly clear the challenge) after a successful verifyOtp, mirroring requireAndConsumeVerifiedEmail's spend semantics; otherwise, document explicitly that Festival Box OTP verification is a mailbox-liveness check, not a one-submission token.
findings.verification_required: Write and run a targeted test that calls sendOtp then submit twice with the same OTP inside the 5-minute window, to confirm both submissions succeed as this code reading implies (not executed in this pass due to time-boxing; this is a code-reading inference, not a reproduced result).

findings.title: No controller-level test exists for FestivalCouponCopyController
findings.evidence: A recursive find for *Festival* under influora-api/src/test located FestivalCouponCopyServiceTest, FestivalCouponCopyDtosTest, FestivalCouponCopyRepositoryConcurrencyTest and FestivalBoxCouponConstraintIntegrationTest, but no FestivalCouponCopyControllerTest anywhere in the tree.
findings.impact: The controller's documented invariants — always 204 regardless of outcome, and getRemoteAddr()-only IP resolution (explicitly never trusting a raw X-Forwarded-For header, per the controller's own [Kabir M-1/M-2] comment) — are protected only by code comments and the service-layer test, not by an executed web-layer regression test. A future refactor could silently change the response code or start trusting a forwarded header without any test failing.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a MockMvc-based FestivalCouponCopyControllerTest asserting: (1) a well-formed request to a recognized sponsor returns 204 with no body, (2) a well-formed request to an unrecognized sponsor/edition also returns 204 with no body (same response, per the no-enumeration-signal design), (3) a malformed request (failing @Valid) returns 400, and (4) the value passed to the service is httpRequest.getRemoteAddr(), not a header value.
findings.verification_required: None beyond confirming the test file continues to be absent at merge time; this finding is a direct file-existence check, already verified.
